fb15k237_cqa.description: Complex query answering on the standard FB15k-237 benchmark (BetaE query splits, 14 query types): rank the non-trivial answers of each test query, i.e. answers that need at least one fact missing from the observed graph. Paper Tables IV/V (and Table VII for the negation ablation).
fb15k237_cqa.notes: Paper numbers (percent) are recorded unchanged. Gym protocol: the paper's own data and filtered MRR/Hits over non-trivial answers, with these departures: (1) a fixed sample of 2000 test queries per type instead of all test queries; (2) methods submit their top-1000 entities per query and unlisted answers count as reciprocal rank 0; (3) besides the benchmark's easy answers, every entity already reachable on the observed train+valid graph is ignored when ranking (identical to the standard filter for positive types; for negated types it also ignores entities that only fail the negated atom through a held-out fact, so post-hoc removal of graph-reachable entities cannot change a score). lvsa_no_logic / lvsa_wo_lns hold the paper's Table VII ablation values.

mrr_A.description: Filtered MRR (%) over non-trivial answers, averaged over the 14 query types.

mrr_Ap.description: Filtered MRR (%) averaged over the 9 positive (EPFO) query types.

mrr_An.description: Filtered MRR (%) averaged over the 5 query types with negation.

hits1_A.description: Filtered Hits@1 (%) averaged over the 14 query types.

hits1_Ap.description: Filtered Hits@1 (%) averaged over the positive query types.

hits1_An.description: Filtered Hits@1 (%) averaged over the negated query types.

hits3_A.description: Filtered Hits@3 (%) averaged over the 14 query types.

hits10_A.description: Filtered Hits@10 (%) averaged over the 14 query types.

fb15k237_unobservable.description: Complex query answering on FB15k-237+H (Gregucci et al., 2025): only full-inference answers, whose every reasoning path needs held-out facts, are ranked; partial-inference answers are ignored. Includes the deeper 4p and 4i types. Paper Table VI and Fig. 6.
fb15k237_unobservable.notes: Paper numbers (percent) unchanged; mrr_A is the paper's A_H (average over the 14 standard types). The 4p/4i values are approximate, read off Fig. 6. Gym protocol as in fb15k237_cqa with a fixed sample of up to 1000 test queries per type.

mrr_A.description: Filtered MRR (%) over full-inference answers of FB15k-237+H, averaged over the 14 standard query types.

mrr_Ap.description: Same, averaged over the 9 positive query types.

mrr_An.description: Same, averaged over the 5 query types with negation.

hits1_A.description: Filtered Hits@1 (%) on FB15k-237+H, averaged over the 14 standard query types.

hits10_A.description: Filtered Hits@10 (%) on FB15k-237+H, averaged over the 14 standard query types.

mrr_ip.description: Filtered MRR (%) on FB15k-237+H ip queries.

mrr_pi.description: Filtered MRR (%) on FB15k-237+H pi queries.

mrr_up.description: Filtered MRR (%) on FB15k-237+H up queries.

mrr_inp.description: Filtered MRR (%) on FB15k-237+H inp queries.

mrr_pin.description: Filtered MRR (%) on FB15k-237+H pin queries.

mrr_pni.description: Filtered MRR (%) on FB15k-237+H pni queries.

mrr_4p.description: Filtered MRR (%) on FB15k-237+H four-hop path queries.

mrr_4i.description: Filtered MRR (%) on FB15k-237+H four-way intersection queries.

fb15k237_traceability.description: Whether the rankings a method emits for the existential variables of 2p/3p queries identify real intermediate entities on a path to a non-trivial answer, and whether the top intermediate choices and top answer form a valid chain. Paper Table VIII (interpretability / logic fidelity).
fb15k237_traceability.notes: The paper's Table VIII counts an intermediate entity as valid when the remaining sub-query is satisfiable on the full graph; on partially observable queries that is satisfied by any observed neighbour, so a graph lookup scores near 100%. The gym therefore requires the path to reach a non-trivial (held-out) answer. The paper's numbers are not on this scale and are kept under _paper_table_viii; the lvsa entry holds this gym's reproduced reference values.

trace_var_mrr.description: Mean reciprocal rank (%) of the first valid intermediate entity in each existential variable's ranking (2p V1, 3p V1, 3p V2 averaged); valid = lies on a full-graph path from the anchor to a non-trivial answer.

trace_var_p1.description: Precision at 1 (%) of the same intermediate rankings.

trace_path_p1.description: Fraction (%) of 2p/3p queries whose top intermediate entities and top non-trivial answer form a valid full-graph reasoning chain ending at a non-trivial answer (2p and 3p averaged).

_paper_table_viii.protocol: satisfiability of the remaining sub-query on the full graph (paper), FB15k-237, percent; averages over 2p V1, 3p V1, 3p V2 (variable level) and 2p, 3p (path level)

_paper_efficiency.note: Not scored: the gym metrics may not depend on wall-clock time, and inference cost cannot be recomputed from submitted rankings. Paper Sec. VI-D, FB15k-237 existential positive queries.
_paper_efficiency.lvsa_vs_cqd_beam: matches CQD-Beam MRR for beam 64-256 with 2-15x higher QPS; CQD-Beam runs out of memory for beam >= 512 with k > 2
_paper_efficiency.complexity: LVSA O(k d^2 + |V| d) per query versus O(|V|^(k+1) d) for exhaustive grounding
